title: Bitune: Leveraging Bidirectional Attention to Improve Decoder-Only LLMs
authors: Dawid J. Kopiczko, Tijmen Blankevoort, Yuki M. Asano
lab: v2: Fundamental AI Lab, University of Technology Nuremberg; Meta (Blankevoort). v1: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Meta, University of Amsterdam
date: arXiv v1 23 May 2024 ("Bitune: Bidirectional Instruction-Tuning"); v2 28 August 2025; EMNLP November 2025

code.title: dkopi/bitune
code.note: the authors' research code (README and passes.py, about 20 minutes): enough to reproduce the paper, by its own README; no licence file, and the promised clean release has not appeared (checked 3 October 2026)

takeaway: The causal mask is required by generation, not by prompt processing. Bitune reads the prompt twice (causal and bidirectional, each with its own adapter), mixes the two sets of keys and values per block with learned weights, and generates causally as usual: +0.1 to +4.0 points over LoRA on five models, for about 3 times the finetuning time.
verdict: Believe the direction: the gains are measured over 3 seeds, survive the noise on most models and in a parameter-matched baseline, and the learning rate was tuned for the baseline, not for Bitune. Treat the size as model-dependent (from +4.0 points on Gemma-2B to +0.1 on Gemma-7B), the claim that every component is needed as not shown (two of the ten ablation gaps are inside the noise), and the cost as larger than "negligible" whenever prompts are long and answers short.
